task.description: Hard-gate REQ-215 on idiomatic OTP usage, supervision integrity, scope creep, and decision-record consistency. Specifically judge SECURITY-REVIEWER's referred question: whether the two-commit (not one-commit) shape between attempt_dispatch/2's terminal-status write and advance_after_service_task_outcome/4's own commit is an acceptable, well-justified divergence from the requirement's literal wording, or a real gap requiring escalation.

result.summary: PASS. Judged the two-commit atomicity divergence acceptable: it is a real, load-bearing constraint forced by REQ-214's own settled scope boundary (ServiceTaskDispatcher may never call Letflow.Engine.*) composed with REQ-215's own explicit 'no change to REQ-214's dispatcher/poller internals' -- poll_and_dispatch/1's reduce loop is the only available call site, necessarily after attempt_dispatch/2's transaction closes. The crash-window gap is real but bounded (a stuck-instance symptom, not silent corruption) and symmetric with the :advance path. Confirmed no supervision-tree changes (pure engine wiring). Confirmed scope discipline held (no change to service_catalog.ex, no route/controller file, ServiceTaskDispatcher's existing function bodies unmodified). Confirmed AC6 purity (zero real :httpc/HTTPoison/Req/File call sites) and moduledoc update. Found 2 non-blocking cleanup items: a bare = match on tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 inside a Multi.merge lambda inconsistent with the module's own with/<- idiom (engine.ex:3297), and a misleadingly-named shared helper (prepare_service_task_dispatch_for_timer_fired/5, actually shared by two hop chains not TIMER-specific). Both applied directly by ORCH per ORCHESTRATOR.md Section 10's sizing rule (renamed to prepare_service_task_dispatch_abort_on_empty_url/5, converted the bare match to with/Multi.error) and re-verified (compile clean, full suite 3119/3119 at that point).
